source.title: Dynamic Regularized Sharpness Aware Minimization in Federated Learning: Approaching Global Consistency and Smooth Landscape
source.authors: Y. Sun; Li Shen; Shi-Xiang Chen; Liang Ding; Da-Cheng Tao

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Compares federated optimizers on held-out classification accuracy and measures Hessian properties, using different settings from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies federated learning on heterogeneous CIFAR splits, not fitting random labels or the train-test gap on natural data. FedAdam's held-out accuracies bear on V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison. Hessian measurements describe flatness but do not measure the magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or train-test gap specified by V7.
record.test_reason: FedAdam versus FedAvg test accuracies bear on V4 in a new setting: federated image classification with server-side adaptivity, local SGD, heterogeneous data and partial participation. The Hessian measurements do not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase captures the authors' conclusion: FedSMOO combines dynamic regularization with a corrected global SAM objective, with claimed fast convergence and improved generalization, especially under severe heterogeneity. Its empirical superiority is not universal: MoFedSAM slightly exceeds it on CIFAR-100 Dirichlet-0.6 at both participation settings.
record.recipe_differences: Federated optimization with partial client participation and non-IID CIFAR data; compares FedAdam as a server-side adaptive optimizer. It does not use the original benchmark recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: CIFAR dataset and split heterogeneity change the relative FedAdam and FedAvg test accuracies.

fits_no_version.finding: FedSMOO has lower Hessian top eigenvalues than FedSAM on both CIFAR-10 Dirichlet splits: 91.46 versus 142.65 and 107.44 versus 177.18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FedSMOO produces lower Hessian top eigenvalues than FedSAM in these federated settings; this does not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202, 2023)
record.problems: Only two runs per Table 1 result; FedAdam comparisons do not report training accuracy or loss. The Hessian comparison does not measure the train-test gap or magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Table 1 contains additional optimizer results, but they are not separately extracted because the claim's tested version concerns adaptive optimizers and the measured FedAdam rows cover that comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and learned local connectivity.

Centralized and language benchmarks; a readable matched training-performance comparison; systematic broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; word-level language models. Appendix B.4 does not fully specify FedAdam's tuning search.
Batch-size effects at fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, correlation with train-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Eight FedAdam-versus-FedAvg accuracy rows for 5% participation among 200 clients. In Table 1 column order, FedAdam/FedAvg values are 75.55±.38/75.90±.21, 69.70±.32/72.93±.19, 75.24±.22/77.47±.34, 70.49±.26/71.86±.34, 44.33±.26/44.70±.22, 38.04±.25/40.41±.33, 35.14±.16/38.22±.25 and 30.28±.28/36.79±.32. These are additional conditions for the extracted optimizer, not merely additional optimizers covered by rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted Table 1 values are correct. Seven of eight extracted conditions favor FedAvg, not six of seven. V4 concerns an often-occurring disadvantage, so the reversed condition does not refute its overall frequency claim. Server-side FedAdam results do not isolate centralized Adam's implicit generalization behavior. Appendix loss curves are not readable enough in the supplied text to establish matched training performance.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Non-federated image and language benchmarks, training performance comparison, broader tuning, weight-decay recovery, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptation.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
No magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or train-test gap measurement; Hessian results are recorded under fits_no_version.
Removing memorized examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.
